blocks.title: Privacy, Data Roles, and Retention comparison
Privacy, Data Roles, and Retention exam shortcuts
items: Question asks who the personal data describes → DATA SUBJECT
The data subject is the individual the information is about.
Example: The customer whose profile is stored.
Who decides why and how data is processed? → CONTROLLER
The controller determines purpose and means.
Example: Retailer decides why it collects customer addresses.
Who handles data for the controller? → PROCESSOR
Processors act on the controller's behalf.
Example: Cloud provider stores customer records.
Need to know what data exists and where → DATA INVENTORY
Inventory documents data assets and locations.
Example: Catalog lists databases containing personal information.
Question asks how long records are kept → RETENTION
Retention rules define the storage period.
Example: Financial records kept for seven years.
Individual asks for lawful deletion of their personal data → RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN
Where applicable, the organization must support deletion requests.
Example: Customer asks the company to erase their account data.
Privacy requirement depends on jurisdiction → LOCAL / NATIONAL / GLOBAL
Determine which legal scope applies.
Example: A multinational company may have obligations in several countries.
blocks.example: Focus on whether the scenario is about proving compliance, maintaining compliance, consequences of failure, or privacy/data-handling responsibilities.

questions.q: A customer's personal information is stored in a company's database. What is the customer called in privacy terminology?
questions.explanation: The data subject is the individual the personal data is about.

questions.q: A retailer decides why customer addresses are collected and how they will be used. Which role is the retailer acting as?
questions.explanation: The controller determines the purposes and means of processing personal data.

questions.q: A payroll company processes employee data on behalf of another organization. Which role is the payroll company acting as?
questions.explanation: A processor handles personal data on behalf of the controller.

questions.q: A company needs to know what personal data it holds, where it is stored, and which team owns it. What should it maintain?
questions.explanation: A data inventory documents what data exists, where it is stored, and who is responsible for it.

questions.q: A regulation requires financial records to be retained for seven years. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Data retention defines how long records must or may be kept.

questions.q: A customer submits a legally valid request for deletion of their personal information. Which privacy concept applies?
questions.explanation: The right to be forgotten may allow an individual to request deletion of personal data when legally applicable.

questions.q: A company operates in several countries and must account for privacy obligations in each jurisdiction. Which scope best describes this?
questions.explanation: Global privacy considerations apply when operating across multiple jurisdictions.
